Where the savings come from

Administrative time handed off
Your hours × your loaded rate × the share you'd hand off. Businesses using a PEO save an average of $965 per employee per year in internal HR salaries and benefits alone — NAPEO / McBassi & Co., The ROI of Using a PEO.

Turnover prevented

How auditors treat subcontractors (NCCI Basic Manual Rule 2)
Insured sub — valid COI / WC certificate on file: excluded from your audit. Adds $0.
Uninsured sub — no COI (default): charged on 100% of what you paid them, unless you provide invoices splitting labor vs. materials.

Introduction
About This Handbook

This Employee Handbook is issued by Sample 1 (referred to throughout as “the Company”). It is effective Sample 2 and applies to all employees. Questions about any policy may be directed to Sample text 4 Second line 4.

This handbook is designed to acquaint you with the Company and provide information about working conditions, benefits, and policies affecting your employment. You should read, understand, and comply with all provisions of the handbook. It describes many of your responsibilities as an employee and outlines the programs the Company has developed to benefit you.

No handbook can anticipate every circumstance or question. As the Company continues to grow, the need may arise to revise, supplement, or rescind policies, or to adopt new ones. The Company reserves the right to do so at any time, with or without notice, except for its policy of at-will employment. This handbook is not a contract of employment and does not create contractual rights of any kind.

Section 1 — Governing Principles of Employment
Welcome Statement

Welcome to the Company. Whether you are beginning your employment or have been with us for some time, we are glad you are part of our team. Our employees provide the service and quality our customers rely on, and your contribution helps us grow and create new opportunities in the years ahead.

Definitions

The term “Company” refers to your employer. The term “employee” refers to a person employed by the Company. The term “Human Resources” refers to the Company's Human Resources function or the individual designated to perform that role.

Equal Employment Opportunity

The Company is an equal opportunity employer. It guarantees every applicant and employee equal treatment without regard to race (including traits historically associated with race, such as hair texture and protective hairstyles), color, religion, creed, sex (including pregnancy, childbirth, and related medical conditions), sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, national origin, ancestry, citizenship, age, physical or mental disability, medical condition, genetic information, marital status, veteran or military status, or any other characteristic protected by federal, state, or local law.

This policy applies to all terms and conditions of employment, including recruitment, hiring, placement, promotion, transfer, training, compensation, benefits, and separation. Employees with questions or concerns about equal employment opportunity are encouraged to contact Human Resources. The Company prohibits retaliation against anyone who raises a good-faith concern under this policy.

Background Checks & Fair Chance Hiring
OPTIONAL

The Company may conduct background checks on applicants and employees where permitted by law and relevant to the position. Any consumer report is obtained only after separate written disclosure and authorization, as required by the Fair Credit Reporting Act.

Consistent with applicable “ban the box” and fair chance laws, the Company does not ask about criminal history on the initial application and does not consider criminal history until after a conditional offer of employment has been made. A criminal record does not automatically disqualify an applicant. Where a record is considered, the Company performs an individualized assessment of the nature and gravity of the offense, the time that has passed, and the relationship of the offense to the duties of the position.

If the Company intends to take adverse action based in whole or in part on a background report, the applicant or employee will receive advance notice, a copy of the report, a summary of rights, and a reasonable opportunity to respond or provide evidence of rehabilitation before a final decision is made.

Disability & Religious Accommodation

Consistent with the Americans with Disabilities Act and applicable state law, the Company will provide reasonable accommodation to a qualified employee or applicant with a known disability, unless doing so would cause undue hardship. The Company will likewise reasonably accommodate an employee's sincerely held religious beliefs or practices absent undue hardship.

An employee who needs an accommodation should notify Human Resources, preferably in writing. The Company will engage in a good-faith interactive process to identify an effective accommodation. The Company makes the final determination as to which reasonable accommodation, if any, will be provided.

Pregnancy, Childbirth & Related Conditions

The Company provides reasonable accommodations to qualified employees and applicants for known limitations related to pregnancy, childbirth, or related medical conditions, as required by the Pregnant Workers Fairness Act and applicable state law, unless doing so would impose an undue hardship.

Accommodations are determined through an interactive discussion between the employee and Sample text 4 Second line 4. Examples may include additional or longer breaks, seating, closer parking, flexible scheduling, temporary reassignment or light duty, limits on lifting, remote work where the job permits, and leave when no other accommodation is effective. An employee will not be required to accept an accommodation without discussion, and will not be forced to take leave if another reasonable accommodation would allow the employee to keep working.

Under the PUMP Act, the Company provides reasonable break time and a private space — other than a bathroom — that is shielded from view and free from intrusion, for an employee to express breast milk for one year after the child's birth. See also the Lactation Accommodation policy.

Retaliation against any employee who requests or uses an accommodation under this policy is prohibited.

Lactation Accommodation

The Company provides reasonable break time and a private space, other than a restroom, for an employee to express breast milk for a nursing child, in accordance with federal and applicable state law. Employees who need this accommodation should contact Human Resources. The Company prohibits retaliation against employees who exercise their rights under this policy.

At-Will Employment

Employment with the Company is at-will. This means that either you or the Company may end the employment relationship at any time, for any reason or no reason, with or without cause or notice, subject to applicable law. No supervisor, manager, or representative of the Company, other than its highest-ranking officer, has authority to alter the at-will relationship or to enter into an agreement for employment for a specified period, and any such agreement must be in writing and signed. Nothing in this handbook limits either party's right to terminate the employment relationship at will.

Anti-Harassment, Discrimination & Retaliation

The Company is committed to a work environment free of harassment, discrimination, and retaliation. It prohibits harassment and discrimination based on any characteristic protected by law, including sexual harassment. Prohibited conduct includes unwelcome advances, requests for favors, slurs, jokes, intimidation, and other verbal, visual, or physical conduct that creates an intimidating, hostile, or offensive work environment.

Any employee who believes they have experienced or witnessed harassment, discrimination, or retaliation should report it promptly to their supervisor or Human Resources. All complaints will be investigated promptly and as confidentially as practical, and appropriate corrective action will be taken. The Company strictly prohibits retaliation against anyone who reports a concern in good faith or participates in an investigation. Employees may also file a charge with the federal Equal Employment Opportunity Commission (EEOC) or the applicable state agency.

Open Door Policy

The Company encourages open, honest communication. If you have a concern about your work, a policy, or a decision, you are encouraged to raise it first with your supervisor. If that is not appropriate or does not resolve the matter, you may take it to the next level of management or to Human Resources. Most concerns can be resolved by discussing them openly.

Whistleblower Protection & Anti-Retaliation

Employees are encouraged and expected to report, in good faith, any conduct they reasonably believe violates a law, regulation, or Company policy — including suspected fraud, theft, falsification of records, unsafe working conditions, discrimination or harassment, wage violations, or environmental violations. Reports may be made to a supervisor, to Sample text 4 Second line 4, or to any member of management.

The Company prohibits retaliation of any kind against an employee who makes a good faith report, who participates in an investigation, who refuses to participate in activity the employee reasonably believes is unlawful, or who exercises any right protected by law. Retaliation includes termination, demotion, discipline, reduction in hours or pay, reassignment, threats, and exclusion.

Nothing in this handbook limits an employee's right to report suspected violations directly to a government agency — including the EEOC, OSHA, the Department of Labor, the NLRB, the SEC, or a state equivalent — or to participate in an agency proceeding. Employees do not need Company permission and are not required to notify the Company first. An employee who believes retaliation has occurred should report it to Sample text 4 Second line 4 immediately; retaliation is itself a violation of this policy and is subject to discipline up to and including termination.

Respect for Others

The Company values healthy, respectful working relationships. Employees are expected to treat one another, and customers, with courtesy and professionalism. Disrespectful behavior — including spreading rumors, making untruthful or malicious statements about others, or similar conduct — undermines the workplace and may result in discipline, up to and including termination.

Drug- and Alcohol-Free Workplace

To protect the safety and productivity of all employees, the Company maintains a workplace free of illegal drugs and alcohol misuse. The unlawful use, possession, sale, or distribution of illegal drugs, and reporting to work under the influence of alcohol or illegal drugs, are prohibited. Employees taking prescription or over-the-counter medication that may impair job performance or safety must notify their supervisor. Violation of this policy may result in discipline, up to and including termination, consistent with applicable law.

Workplace Violence Prevention

The Company is committed to a safe workplace and does not tolerate threats, threatening behavior, intimidation, or acts of violence by or against employees, customers, or visitors. Weapons are prohibited on Company premises to the extent permitted by law. Any threat or act of violence should be reported immediately to management. Reports made in good faith will not result in retaliation, and all reports will be investigated. Violations may result in discipline, up to and including termination, and referral to law enforcement.

Right to Revise

This handbook contains the Company's current employment policies. Except for the policy of at-will employment, the Company reserves the right to revise, modify, delete, or add to any policy, procedure, work rule, or benefit at any time, with or without notice. Written changes supersede prior policy. No oral statement can alter the provisions of this handbook.

Section 2 — Workplace & Compensation
Employee Classifications

Each employee is classified as full-time, part-time, or temporary/seasonal, and as either exempt or non-exempt under federal and state wage-and-hour law. Non-exempt employees are entitled to overtime and any legally required meal and rest breaks; exempt employees are not eligible for overtime. Benefit eligibility depends on classification. Your classification does not change your at-will status. You will be told your classification at hire and of any later change.

Introductory Period

The beginning of employment is an introductory period during which you and the Company can evaluate whether the position is a good fit. The Company may extend this period at its discretion. Completing the introductory period does not change your at-will status or create any guarantee of continued employment.

Job Duties

Your supervisor will explain your job responsibilities and the standards expected of you. Job duties may change over time, and you may be asked to perform additional or different work as needed. The Company may alter job responsibilities, reassign positions, or add duties at any time, with or without notice.

Personnel Records

The Company maintains a personnel file for each employee. You are responsible for keeping your information current — including address, telephone number, emergency contact, and tax-withholding details — by notifying Human Resources of any change. Accurate records are important for pay, benefits, and reaching you in an emergency.

Employment Eligibility Verification (Form I-9)

Federal law requires the Company to verify the identity and employment authorization of every person hired. Each new employee must complete Section 1 of Form I-9 no later than the first day of work and present acceptable original documentation within three business days of the start date. Employees choose which acceptable documents to present; the Company does not specify or demand particular documents, and does not request more or different documents than the law requires.

Where an employee's employment authorization document carries an expiration date, the Company will reverify authorization on or before the expiration date. The Company does not reverify U.S. passports, Permanent Resident Cards, or List B identity documents. Employees are asked to provide updated documentation in advance to avoid an interruption in work.

The Company complies with the anti-discrimination provisions of the Immigration and Nationality Act. It does not treat employees differently in hiring, verification, or reverification on the basis of citizenship status or national origin, and does not retaliate against an employee for asserting rights under those provisions.

Employment References & Verification
OPTIONAL

All requests for employment verification or references — from lenders, prospective employers, background screening firms, or government agencies — must be directed to Sample text 4 Second line 4. Supervisors and coworkers should not respond to reference requests on the Company's behalf.

Unless the employee provides written authorization to release more, the Company confirms only dates of employment, position(s) held, and, where required by law or requested for verification of income, rate of pay. This practice protects both the employee and the Company and ensures that information released is accurate and consistent.

Work Schedules, Meal & Rest Breaks

You will be assigned a work schedule and are expected to begin and end work accordingly. Business needs may require schedule changes. Non-exempt employees must take any meal and rest breaks required by applicable state law; specific requirements are described in the State-Specific Supplement to this handbook. Employees must be fully relieved of duty during unpaid meal periods. If you are ever unable to take a required break, notify your supervisor or Human Resources promptly.

Timekeeping

Non-exempt employees must accurately record all time worked, including the start and end of each shift and of any unpaid meal period, using the Company's timekeeping system. Working “off the clock” is prohibited, and no supervisor may ask you to do so. Falsifying or altering time records is prohibited and may result in discipline, up to and including termination. Report any timekeeping error to your supervisor right away.

Overtime

Non-exempt employees are paid overtime as required by federal and applicable state law — generally one-and-one-half times the regular rate for hours worked over 40 in a workweek. Some states also require daily overtime; where that applies, it is described in the State-Specific Supplement. Overtime must be authorized in advance by management. Unauthorized overtime will be paid but may result in discipline.

Meal & Rest Periods

Non-exempt employees are provided meal and rest periods in accordance with federal and state law. Where state law requires them, meal periods are generally at least thirty minutes and rest periods at least ten minutes for every four hours worked or major fraction thereof. Specific requirements for your work location appear in the State-Specific Supplement.

Meal periods are unpaid and duty-free. An employee must be fully relieved of all duties and free to leave the work area. An employee who is interrupted, asked to remain on duty, or unable to take a full meal period must report this to a supervisor the same day so the time is paid correctly. Rest periods are paid and count as time worked; they may not be combined with a meal period, used to arrive late or leave early, or accumulated.

Working through a meal or rest period without authorization is not permitted. An employee who does so will be paid for the time and may be subject to discipline for failing to follow this policy.

Paychecks & Deductions

You will be paid on the Company's regular payroll schedule. Your pay statement itemizes gross earnings and all deductions, including legally required taxes and withholdings. The Company complies with federal and state law regarding wage deductions. If you believe there is an error in your pay, report it to Human Resources or payroll immediately so it can be corrected; the Company prohibits retaliation for raising a good-faith pay concern.

Pay Transparency & Wage Discussions

Employees have the right to inquire about, discuss, and disclose their own wages and the wages of other employees. The Company will not discharge, discipline, or otherwise retaliate against an employee for doing so, and no policy, agreement, or instruction from a supervisor may be interpreted to prohibit such discussions. Employees whose regular job duties give them access to compensation information may not disclose that information without authorization, except as permitted by law.

Where required by state or local law, the Company discloses the pay scale or wage range for a position in the job posting, on request from an applicant, and on request from a current employee for the employee's own position. The Company does not ask applicants about salary history where that inquiry is prohibited by law, and does not rely on salary history to set pay.

Pay decisions are based on job-related factors including experience, skill, education, certifications, performance, geography, and market data. Any employee who believes a pay decision was made on a basis prohibited by law should raise it with Sample text 4 Second line 4.

Payroll Errors & Improper Deduction Safe Harbor
OPTIONAL

The Company intends to pay every employee accurately and on time, and to comply with the salary basis requirements for exempt employees. Improper deductions from an exempt employee's salary are prohibited.

An employee who believes a paycheck is incorrect — whether an underpayment, an overpayment, an unauthorized deduction, or missing hours — should report it to Sample text 4 Second line 4 immediately. The Company will investigate promptly, and any improper deduction or underpayment confirmed will be reimbursed on the next regular payroll or sooner where required by law. An employee will not be retaliated against for reporting a suspected payroll error.

Where an overpayment has occurred, the Company will notify the employee, explain the amount and cause, and arrange repayment on terms consistent with applicable law. Deductions to recover an overpayment are made only with the employee's written authorization where such authorization is required.

Wage Garnishments & Support Orders
OPTIONAL

The Company is required by law to honor valid garnishment orders, child support withholding orders, tax levies, and similar legal process. When such an order is received, the Company will notify the affected employee, provide a copy of the order where permitted, and begin withholding on the schedule the order requires.

The Company withholds only the amount the order and applicable law allow, applies the limits of the Consumer Credit Protection Act and any stricter state limit, and will not disclose the existence of an order to coworkers. An employee will not be discharged because wages are garnished for any one indebtedness. Questions about the underlying debt must be directed to the issuing court or agency; the Company cannot modify, delay, or contest the order on an employee's behalf.

Expense Reimbursement

The Company reimburses employees for reasonable, necessary, and pre-approved business expenses incurred in performing their jobs, consistent with applicable law and Company procedure. Submit required receipts and an expense form promptly. Employees should obtain approval before incurring a significant business expense, and should contact their supervisor with any questions about reimbursement.

Attendance & Punctuality
OPTIONAL

Regular attendance and punctuality are essential. If you will be late or absent, notify your supervisor as early as possible in accordance with Company call-in procedures. Excessive absenteeism or tardiness, or failure to notify the Company, may result in discipline, up to and including termination. Absences protected by law will be handled in accordance with the applicable leave policy.

Section 3 — Benefits & Time Off
Benefits Overview

The Company offers a range of benefits to eligible employees. This handbook summarizes them in general terms only. The specific terms, eligibility, and conditions of each benefit plan are governed by the official plan documents and insurance contracts, which control in the event of any difference with this handbook. The Company may change, add, or discontinue benefits at any time consistent with applicable law and plan terms.

When You Can Enroll
OPTIONAL

There are three times you can enroll in or change your benefits.

When you are first eligible. New employees may enroll during the initial enrollment window described in your offer or benefits summary. If you do not enroll during that window, you must wait for open enrollment unless you have a qualifying life event.

Open enrollment. Once a year the Company holds an open enrollment period. This is the one time you can add, drop or change coverage for any reason. Elections made during open enrollment take effect on the first day of the new plan year and generally cannot be changed until the following year.

A qualifying life event. Certain life changes let you change coverage mid-year — see the next section. You generally have 30 days from the event to make the change, and the Company may require documentation.

If you take no action during open enrollment, your current elections may carry forward or may default to no coverage, depending on the plan. Read the enrollment materials each year; do not assume.

Health & Insurance Benefits

Eligible employees may participate in the Company's health and related insurance benefits, subject to the terms of the applicable plans. Human Resources can provide summary plan descriptions and enrollment information. Continuation of coverage after certain qualifying events may be available under COBRA or applicable state continuation law.

Understanding Your Benefits — Plain English
OPTIONAL

Benefits paperwork is full of terms that are rarely explained. Here is what they actually mean.

Premium — what the coverage costs each pay period, whether or not you use it. Your share is deducted from your paycheck.

Deductible — what you pay out of pocket each plan year before the plan starts paying its share. A $2,000 deductible means the first $2,000 of covered care is yours.

Copay — a flat amount for a specific service, such as $30 to see a doctor. Copays often apply before you meet the deductible.

Coinsurance — after the deductible, the percentage you keep paying. “80/20” means the plan pays 80% and you pay 20%.

Out-of-pocket maximum — the most you can pay in a plan year. Once you reach it, the plan pays 100% of covered in-network care. This is the number that protects you from a catastrophe.

In-network — providers who agreed to discounted rates. Going out of network costs dramatically more, and sometimes is not covered at all. Check before you book.

HSA and FSA — accounts that let you pay medical costs with pre-tax dollars. An HSA requires a high-deductible plan, the money is yours permanently and it rolls over. An FSA does not require a specific plan, but is largely use-it-or-lose-it within the plan year.

Continuation of Health Coverage (COBRA)
OPTIONAL

When Company-sponsored group health coverage would otherwise end because of a qualifying event, an employee and covered dependents may have the right to continue that coverage for a limited period at their own expense under COBRA or a comparable state continuation law.

Qualifying events include termination of employment for reasons other than gross misconduct, a reduction in hours below the eligibility threshold, divorce or legal separation, a dependent child aging out of the plan, and the death of the employee. The Company will provide an election notice through the plan administrator following a qualifying event. The employee or dependent is responsible for notifying Sample text 4 Second line 4 within sixty days of a divorce, legal separation, or a child ceasing to be eligible.

Continuation coverage is identical to the coverage in place before the qualifying event, and the individual pays the full premium plus any permitted administrative fee. Election and payment deadlines are strict; missing them ends the right to continue coverage. Complete details are in the plan's Summary Plan Description, which controls in the event of any conflict with this summary.

Retirement / 401(k)
OPTIONAL

The Company may offer a retirement savings plan to eligible employees. Details regarding eligibility, contributions, and any Company match are described in the official plan documents, available from Human Resources.

Holidays
OPTIONAL

The Company observes a schedule of paid holidays for eligible employees. The current holiday schedule is provided separately and may be updated from time to time. Eligibility and pay for holidays depend on your classification and Company policy.

Paid Time Off Donation & Leave Sharing
OPTIONAL

The Company may permit employees to donate accrued paid time off to a coworker who has exhausted their own accrued time and is facing a qualifying medical emergency, a serious illness of the employee or a family member, or a federally declared disaster.

Donations are voluntary and confidential. A donating employee submits a written request to Sample text 4 Second line 4 specifying the number of hours; donations are irrevocable once transferred and may be capped to ensure the donor retains a reasonable reserve. Donated time is converted to the recipient's rate of pay and is paid as ordinary wages subject to withholding.

No employee will be pressured to donate, and no supervisor may solicit donations from direct reports. The Company reviews each request individually and may decline where the circumstances do not meet the criteria or where the program's tax treatment would be jeopardized.

Paid Sick Leave

Where required by state or local law, the Company provides paid sick leave to eligible employees. The specific accrual, caps, and permitted uses that apply to your location are described in the State-Specific Supplement to this handbook. The Company prohibits retaliation against employees for lawfully using protected sick leave.

Workers' Compensation

The Company carries workers' compensation insurance as required by law to cover employees who suffer a work-related injury or illness. Report any work-related injury or illness to your supervisor immediately, no matter how minor, so that a timely claim can be filed. It is unlawful, and against Company policy, to retaliate against an employee for filing a good-faith workers' compensation claim.

Section 4 — Leaves of Absence
Family & Medical Leave

If the Company is covered by the federal Family and Medical Leave Act (FMLA), eligible employees may take unpaid, job-protected leave for qualifying family and medical reasons, including the birth or placement of a child, a serious health condition of the employee or a family member, and certain military-family needs. Many states also provide family or medical leave rights that may be broader than federal law; those are described in the State-Specific Supplement. Contact Human Resources to request leave and for details on eligibility and coordination with other benefits.

Military Leave (USERRA)

The Company grants military leave and reemployment rights in accordance with the Uniformed Services Employment and Reemployment Rights Act (USERRA) and applicable state law. Employees who need leave for military service should notify Human Resources as far in advance as possible. The Company does not discriminate or retaliate against employees because of their military service or obligations.

Domestic Violence, Sexual Assault & Crime Victim Leave
OPTIONAL

An employee who is a victim of domestic violence, sexual assault, stalking, or another crime, or whose family member is a victim, may take leave to obtain medical care or counseling, seek a restraining or protective order, attend court or law enforcement proceedings, relocate, or take other steps to ensure safety. The length of leave, whether it is paid, and which family relationships qualify vary by state; the requirements for your work location appear in the State-Specific Supplement.

An employee should give as much notice as is practicable. Where advance notice is not possible, certification may be provided afterward — for example a police report, a court record, or documentation from a health care provider, counselor, or victim services organization. The Company will accept an employee's written statement where a state permits it.

All information related to a request under this policy is kept confidential and disclosed only as required by law or as necessary to protect the safety of the employee or others. The Company will also consider reasonable safety accommodations, such as a schedule change, a transfer, a new work telephone number, or changes to a worksite entrance. Retaliation against an employee for requesting or taking leave under this policy is prohibited.

Jury Duty & Witness Leave
OPTIONAL

The Company grants time off for jury duty and to respond to a lawful subpoena as required by law. Notify your supervisor promptly when you receive a summons. Whether such leave is paid is determined by Company policy and applicable state law. The Company will not penalize an employee for serving.

Bereavement Leave
OPTIONAL

The Company provides bereavement leave to eligible employees following the death of a family member, in accordance with Company policy and any applicable state law. Contact your supervisor or Human Resources to arrange leave.

Voting Leave
OPTIONAL

The Company supports employees' right to vote. Where required by state law, the Company provides time off to vote. If you believe you will not have sufficient time to vote outside working hours, notify your supervisor in advance so arrangements can be made.

Section 5 — Standards of Conduct
Standards of Conduct

To protect the interests of all employees and the Company, certain standards of conduct are necessary. Conduct that may result in discipline, up to and including termination, includes but is not limited to: dishonesty, theft, insubordination, violation of safety rules, harassment or discrimination, unauthorized use of Company property, falsification of records, being under the influence of drugs or alcohol at work, excessive absenteeism, and violation of Company policy. This list is illustrative, not exhaustive. Because employment is at-will, the Company may discipline or terminate for any lawful reason.

Protected Rights — Savings Clause

Nothing in this handbook is intended to interfere with, restrain, or prevent employees from exercising rights protected by Section 7 of the National Labor Relations Act, and no policy in this handbook will be interpreted or applied in a way that does so.

Employees have the right to engage in protected concerted activity — to organize, to form, join, or assist a labor organization, to bargain collectively through representatives of their own choosing, and to act together with other employees for mutual aid or protection regarding wages, hours, and other terms and conditions of employment. Employees also have the right to refrain from any of these activities.

Accordingly, no provision of this handbook — including the policies on conduct, confidentiality, technology, social media, solicitation, recording, media contact, or complaint procedures — prohibits employees from discussing wages, benefits, working conditions, safety, or terms of employment with each other, with a union, with the news media, or with a government agency; from raising work-related concerns publicly or on social media; from wearing or displaying union insignia where otherwise permitted; or from participating in a Board proceeding or investigation.

If any part of this handbook conflicts with rights protected by the Act or by any other federal, state, or local law, this savings clause controls and the conflicting part will not be enforced.

Confidentiality

During employment you may have access to confidential and proprietary information about the Company, its customers, and its employees. You must keep such information confidential and use it only for legitimate business purposes, both during and after your employment. Nothing in this policy limits your right to discuss wages, hours, or other terms and conditions of employment, or to engage in other legally protected activity.

Employee Data Privacy
OPTIONAL

The Company collects and maintains personal information about employees as necessary to administer employment — including identification and contact details, government identifiers, compensation and tax data, benefits elections, emergency contacts, time and attendance records, and performance documentation.

This information is used only for legitimate business and legal purposes: payroll and tax reporting, benefits administration, workers' compensation, safety, compliance with legal obligations, and management of the employment relationship. Access is limited to those with a business need. The Company does not sell employee personal information, and shares it with third parties — such as payroll providers, insurers, and benefit administrators — only as required to deliver those services, under agreements that limit further use.

The Company retains employee records for the periods required by law and disposes of them securely. Employees in states with employee privacy statutes have additional rights, including the right to know what categories of information are collected and the right to request correction or deletion where the law permits; those rights and how to exercise them appear in the State-Specific Supplement. Direct any question or request to Sample text 4 Second line 4.

Outside Employment
OPTIONAL

Employees may hold outside employment or operate a business of their own, provided it does not interfere with their duties here. An employee is expected to disclose outside employment to their supervisor and Sample text 4 Second line 4 so that any conflict can be identified early.

Outside employment is not permitted where it competes with the Company, uses Company time, equipment, supplies, facilities, or confidential information, involves soliciting Company customers or employees, creates a safety risk through fatigue or excessive hours, or impairs the employee's ability to meet performance and attendance standards. Employees may not perform outside work during scheduled working hours.

Nothing in this policy restricts activity protected by law, including protected concerted activity or lawful off-duty conduct where state law protects it. If outside employment begins to interfere with job performance, the employee will be asked to address the conflict, and continued interference may result in discipline.

Company Property

Company property — including equipment, tools, vehicles, devices, and materials — must be used properly, maintained with care, and used only for authorized business purposes. Employees must return all Company property upon separation. The Company reserves the right, to the extent permitted by law, to inspect Company property and premises.

Workplace Searches
OPTIONAL

To protect the safety of employees and the security of Company and customer property, the Company reserves the right to inspect Company property at any time, with or without notice. Company property includes desks, lockers, cabinets, vehicles, tool cribs, work areas, and Company-issued computers, phones, and storage.

Employees should have no expectation of privacy in Company property. Where an employee is permitted to use a personal lock, a duplicate key or combination must be provided to Sample text 4 Second line 4. Personal belongings brought onto Company premises may be inspected where the Company has a reasonable, articulable basis for doing so and where state law permits.

Searches are conducted respectfully, and where practicable in the presence of the employee and a witness. Refusal to cooperate with a lawful search may result in discipline. This policy is not applied on a discriminatory basis and will not be used to interfere with protected activity.

Company Vehicles & Driving
OPTIONAL

An employee who drives a Company vehicle, or a personal vehicle for Company business, must hold a valid driver's license and, where a personal vehicle is used, maintain the insurance coverage required by state law. The employee must notify Sample text 4 Second line 4 immediately if the license is suspended, revoked, or restricted. The Company may review driving records at hire and periodically thereafter where permitted by law.

Company vehicles are for business use. Drivers must obey all traffic laws, wear seat belts, secure loads, complete any required pre-trip inspection, and report mechanical problems promptly. Operating a vehicle while under the influence of alcohol, cannabis, illegal drugs, or any substance that impairs driving is strictly prohibited. Traffic and parking citations are the responsibility of the driver.

Any accident involving a Company vehicle or occurring while on Company business must be reported to a supervisor immediately, regardless of severity or fault, and the driver must remain at the scene, contact law enforcement, and complete the Company's accident report. Drivers subject to DOT regulation must also comply with all applicable federal motor carrier requirements, including hours of service and drug and alcohol testing.

Electronic Communications & Technology

Company systems, email, internet access, and devices are provided for business purposes. Employees should have no expectation of privacy in their use of Company systems, to the extent permitted by law. Use of Company technology must comply with Company policy and the law. This policy is not intended to interfere with employees' legally protected rights to communicate about the terms and conditions of employment.

Personal Devices (BYOD)
OPTIONAL

Employees who are permitted to use a personal phone, tablet, or computer for Company work must first obtain approval from Sample text 4 Second line 4 and agree to the conditions of this policy.

A personal device used for Company work must be protected by a passcode or biometric lock, kept current on operating system and security updates, and encrypted where the device supports it. Company data must be stored only in Company-approved applications and cloud services, not in personal accounts, personal cloud storage, or personal messaging apps. Employees may not disable Company security software or jailbreak or root a device used for work.

Company data on a personal device remains Company property. On separation, or if a device is lost or stolen, the Company may remotely remove Company data and, where that is not technically possible, may require the employee to surrender the device for that purpose. The Company does not monitor personal content, photos, or personal communications on a personal device, and will limit any access to Company data.

A non-exempt employee may not perform work on a personal device outside scheduled hours without advance approval, and must record all such time. The Company reimburses a reasonable portion of the cost of a personal device or service plan used for work where required by state law.

Social Media
OPTIONAL

When using social media, employees are personally responsible for what they post. Do not disclose the Company's confidential information or post anything unlawful, harassing, or that a reasonable person would view as malicious. This policy does not restrict employees' legally protected right to discuss wages, hours, or working conditions.

Dress & Appearance
OPTIONAL

Employees are expected to present a clean, neat, and professional appearance appropriate to their role and to maintain workplace safety standards. The Company will reasonably accommodate dress and grooming practices related to religion, disability, or other protected characteristics as required by law.

Workplace Safety

Safety is everyone's responsibility. Employees must follow all safety rules, use required protective equipment, and report unsafe conditions, injuries, and near-misses promptly. The Company complies with the federal Occupational Safety and Health Act and, where applicable, an OSHA-approved state plan; the applicable authority for your location is noted in the State-Specific Supplement. Retaliation against an employee for raising a good-faith safety concern is prohibited.

Corrective Action
OPTIONAL

The Company may address performance or conduct concerns through corrective action, which may include coaching, verbal or written warnings, suspension, or termination. The Company may use any of these steps, in any order, or none, depending on the circumstances. Nothing in this policy alters the at-will employment relationship, and the Company may terminate employment at any time for any lawful reason.

Remote Work
OPTIONAL

Where the Company permits remote work, it is a privilege granted at the Company's discretion based on role and business needs, not an entitlement. Remote employees must maintain productivity, protect confidential information, remain reachable during working hours, accurately record time if non-exempt, and comply with all Company policies. The Company may modify or end a remote-work arrangement at any time.

State-Specific Supplement — Arkansas
State Law Application
STATE

This handbook is intended for the Company's operations in Arkansas. Where Arkansas law provides employees greater rights or benefits than federal law, Arkansas law controls. Where this handbook and applicable law conflict, the law controls, and the remainder of the handbook stays in effect.

Wages & Overtime
STATE

Non-exempt employees are paid overtime at one-and-one-half times their regular rate for hours worked over 40 in a workweek, in accordance with the federal Fair Labor Standards Act and Arkansas law. Arkansas sets its own minimum wage, which may exceed the federal minimum; the Company pays at least the highest applicable rate.

Meal & Rest Breaks
STATE

Arkansas does not impose a general statewide meal or rest break mandate for adult private-sector employees; the Company provides breaks consistent with federal law and operational needs. Nonexempt employees are relieved of duty during any unpaid meal period.

Final Pay & Pay Frequency
STATE

Arkansas sets rules for how often employees must be paid and how quickly final wages are due after a separation (these deadlines often differ for a discharge versus a resignation). The Company follows the Arkansas deadlines in effect. ⚑ Confirm current figures with counsel or your state labor department before adoption.

State Fair Employment Agency
STATE

In addition to the federal EEOC, employees in Arkansas may have rights under state anti-discrimination law and may contact the Arkansas state fair-employment/civil-rights agency. State law may cover additional protected characteristics and may apply to smaller employers than federal law. ⚑ Confirm current figures with counsel or your state labor department before adoption.

Read this first: when a payroll company sweeps your account, one entry is enough

If your payroll provider (a PEO, ASO or payroll service) pulls one ACH for the whole payroll, your bank shows one number. Your books only need to do two things: match that number, and put the cost where it belongs. That takes one journal entry with a handful of lines: wages, employer taxes and workers comp, the provider's fee, and whatever was withheld that you still have to pay yourself (401(k), health premiums). That is all your tax return and your CPA ever need: wages, payroll taxes and fees as separate totals. Not FICA, FUTA, SUTA, each state, each garnishment or each employee as its own transaction.

Why not break it all out? None of those pieces hit your bank on their own, so posting them separately does not make the books more accurate. It makes reconciliation slower, month end harder, and creates more places for a mistake. If an auditor, a lender or your CPA ever needs the detail (FICA by quarter, a garnishment history, wages by employee), your payroll software prints that report in seconds. The general ledger is not where that detail lives.

If the provider pulls two or three ACHs (say one for net wages, one for taxes and burden, one for the fee), post one bank line per ACH so each one reconciles, and nothing more. The expense side stays the same few lines.

Need job costing or department reporting? Break out the wage expense by department, location, division or job in step 4. That is real information your P&L can use. Breaking it out by tax type is not. This tool defaults to the simple entry; everything else is optional.

Introduction
About This Safety Manual

This Safety Manual is issued by Sample 1 (“the Company”), effective Sample 2. It describes the Company's safety and health program and the responsibilities of every employee. Direct questions to Sample text 4 Second line 4.

The Company is committed to providing a safe and healthful workplace and to complying with the federal Occupational Safety and Health Act (and, where applicable, an OSHA-approved state plan). This manual is a general program document; it does not replace the specific written programs, training, and site-specific procedures that certain hazards require.

Section 1 — Safety Program & Responsibilities
Safety Policy Statement

The safety and health of our employees is a core priority. No task is so urgent that it cannot be done safely. Management is responsible for providing a safe workplace, the necessary training, and appropriate protective equipment. Every employee is responsible for following safe work practices, using required protection, and reporting hazards. Safety is a shared responsibility and a condition of employment.

Roles & Responsibilities

Management ensures resources, training, and enforcement of this program. Supervisors enforce safe practices, correct hazards, investigate incidents, and train their teams. Employees follow all safety rules, use required personal protective equipment (PPE), report hazards, injuries, and near-misses, and never remove or defeat a safety device. A designated safety coordinator maintains records and coordinates the program.

Hazard Identification & Inspections

The Company conducts periodic workplace inspections to identify and correct hazards. Employees are encouraged to report unsafe conditions immediately, without fear of retaliation. Identified hazards are prioritized and corrected, and interim protective measures are used until a permanent fix is in place.

Safety Training

Employees receive safety training at hire, when assigned new tasks or equipment, when hazards change, and periodically thereafter. Training covers this program, job-specific hazards, safe work procedures, and the proper use of PPE. Training is documented and retained.

Return to Work & Modified Duty
OPTIONAL

An injured employee who returns to productive work recovers faster and costs less. Sample 1 maintains a formal return-to-work program and will make every reasonable effort to provide temporary modified or transitional duty to an employee recovering from a work-related injury or illness.

How it works. After a work-related injury, the treating physician is given a written job description and asked to state the employee's specific physical capabilities and restrictions. The Company then identifies temporary work within those restrictions — a modification of the employee's regular job, a reduced schedule, or a different assignment. The offer is made in writing and states the duties, hours, pay, and expected duration.

Terms. Modified duty is temporary, is reviewed at each medical appointment, and generally does not extend beyond ninety days without review by Sample text 4 Second line 4. It is not a permanent position and does not change the employee's regular job classification. Employees are paid for the work performed; where the modified wage is lower than the pre-injury wage, temporary partial disability benefits may apply under the state workers' compensation system.

Employee responsibilities. Attend all scheduled medical appointments, provide the Company with each work status report the same day it is issued, work within the stated restrictions both on and off the job, and report immediately any task that exceeds them. Refusing a bona fide offer of modified duty within the treating physician's restrictions may affect entitlement to wage replacement benefits under state law.

Participation in this program is not an admission of liability, is not discipline, and does not affect an employee's rights under workers' compensation, the ADA, or the FMLA. Where an injury results in a permanent limitation, the Company will engage in the interactive accommodation process separately.

Safety Enforcement

Compliance with safety rules is mandatory. Violations may result in corrective action, up to and including termination, consistent with Company policy and applicable law. Enforcement is applied fairly and consistently. Reporting a safety concern in good faith is protected and will never result in retaliation.

Section 2 — Core OSHA Programs
Written Safety & Health Program

The Company maintains a written safety and health program that establishes responsibility, a system for identifying and correcting hazards, procedures for investigating incidents, safety training, and a means for employees to report hazards. Several states (for example, California's Injury and Illness Prevention Program) require a written program by law; the Company maintains one as a best practice regardless.

Hazard Communication (HazCom / GHS)

Employees who may be exposed to hazardous chemicals are informed and trained under the OSHA Hazard Communication Standard. The Company maintains a chemical inventory, keeps Safety Data Sheets (SDS) accessible to employees, ensures containers are properly labeled under the Globally Harmonized System (GHS), and trains employees on chemical hazards and protective measures.

Personal Protective Equipment (PPE)

Where hazards cannot be eliminated by other means, the Company provides and requires appropriate PPE — such as eye, head, hand, foot, hearing, and respiratory protection. The Company assesses PPE needs by task, trains employees on proper use and care, and requires that PPE be worn as directed. Employees must inspect PPE before use and report damaged equipment.

Emergency Action & Fire Prevention

The Company maintains an Emergency Action Plan covering evacuation routes and procedures, alarm systems, assembly points, and how to report emergencies. Fire prevention measures include control of ignition sources, proper storage of flammables, access to fire extinguishers, and clear exits. Employees are trained on emergency procedures and participate in drills as scheduled.

Injury Reporting & Recordkeeping

Employees must report every work-related injury or illness to their supervisor immediately, no matter how minor. The Company records and reports injuries and illnesses as required by OSHA (including, where covered, the OSHA 300 Log, 300A Summary, and 301 forms) and reports severe incidents to OSHA within required timeframes. Retaliation for reporting an injury is prohibited.

Safety Inspections & Audits
OPTIONAL

Regular inspection is how hazards are found before they cause injury. Sample 1 conducts documented safety inspections on a defined schedule: daily pre-shift walkarounds by the supervisor at each active work area, weekly documented inspections of tools, equipment, and housekeeping, and a comprehensive facility or site audit at least quarterly.

Inspections use a written checklist appropriate to the work being performed. Every finding is recorded with a description of the hazard, its location, an assigned corrective action, a responsible person, and a due date. Imminent hazards are corrected immediately or the area is barricaded and the work stopped. Open items are reviewed at the next safety meeting until closed.

Employees are encouraged to participate in inspections and to report hazards at any time without waiting for a scheduled walk. Inspection records are retained for at least three years and are reviewed for trends — a hazard that appears repeatedly indicates a systemic problem, not an individual failure.

Incident Investigation

The Company investigates injuries, illnesses, and significant near-misses to determine root causes and prevent recurrence. Investigations focus on identifying system and hazard causes rather than assigning blame. Corrective actions are tracked to completion.

Section 3 — Job-Specific Hazard Programs
Lockout/Tagout (Control of Hazardous Energy)
OPTIONAL

Before servicing or maintaining machines or equipment where unexpected energization could cause injury, authorized employees isolate and lock out all hazardous energy sources following written procedures. Only trained, authorized employees perform lockout/tagout. Employees must never operate equipment that is locked or tagged out.

Scaffolding Safety (29 CFR 1926.451)
OPTIONAL

Scaffolds are erected, moved, altered, and dismantled only under the supervision of a competent person qualified in scaffold erection, and only by trained and experienced employees.

Design and capacity. Every scaffold and component supports its own weight plus at least four times the maximum intended load. Scaffolds are erected on base plates and mud sills or another adequate firm foundation, plumb, level, and braced. Scaffolds are not supported by unstable objects such as barrels, boxes, loose brick, or concrete block.

Platforms and access. Platforms are fully planked with no gap greater than one inch between planks or between the platform and uprights. Fall protection is required above ten feet: a guardrail system with a top rail at 38 to 45 inches, a midrail, and toeboards where anyone may pass below, or a personal fall arrest system. Access is by stairway, ladder, ramp, or integral prefabricated frame access — never by climbing cross braces.

Daily inspection. A competent person inspects each scaffold and its components before every work shift and after any event that could affect structural integrity. Damaged parts are removed from service and tagged. Scaffolds are not used during high wind, storms, or when covered with ice or snow unless a competent person determines it is safe and fall protection is in place. Work is stopped and the scaffold cleared when the minimum safe clearance from energized power lines cannot be maintained.

Ladders & Stairways (29 CFR 1926 Subpart X)
OPTIONAL

Ladders are inspected before each use and removed from service if damaged, missing parts, or contaminated with oil or grease. Damaged ladders are tagged and destroyed or repaired to original strength; they are never used in the meantime.

Use. Portable ladders used to access an upper level extend at least three feet above the landing surface and are secured at the top or held. Non-self-supporting ladders are set at a 4-to-1 pitch — one foot out for every four feet of working length. Employees face the ladder, maintain three points of contact, and do not carry loads that could cause a loss of balance. Only one person is on a ladder at a time unless it is designed for more.

Prohibited. Do not stand on the top step or top cap of a stepladder, place a ladder on boxes, barrels, or other unstable bases, use a ladder in a horizontal position as a platform or runway, tie ladders together to gain length, or move a ladder while occupied. Metal and wire-reinforced ladders are never used near energized electrical equipment.

Stairways. Stairways with four or more risers or rising more than thirty inches have a handrail and stair rail system. Treads are kept free of debris, and slippery conditions are corrected before the stairway is used. Temporary stairs are not filled with construction material.

Respiratory Protection
OPTIONAL

Where respiratory hazards are present and cannot be controlled by other means, the Company implements a respiratory protection program including hazard assessment, medical evaluation, fit testing, proper selection, training, and maintenance of respirators, in accordance with the OSHA Respiratory Protection Standard.

Asbestos & Lead Awareness
OPTIONAL

Buildings constructed before 1980 may contain asbestos in insulation, floor tile, mastic, roofing, siding, and pipe wrap, and lead in paint, solder, and plumbing. Disturbing these materials releases fibers or dust that cause serious, often delayed disease.

Presume and stop. Employees treat suspect material in a pre-1980 structure as containing asbestos or lead unless testing proves otherwise. No employee disturbs, cuts, sands, drills, scrapes, burns, or removes suspect material. Work stops and a supervisor is notified immediately if suspect material is discovered or damaged during other work.

Licensed work only. Abatement, removal, and disturbance of asbestos-containing material or lead-based paint is performed only by properly licensed and certified contractors under a separate written compliance program, with the required notifications, containment, air monitoring, and disposal. Sample 1 employees do not perform this work unless specifically trained, certified, and enrolled in medical surveillance.

Renovation rule. Work that disturbs lead-based paint in housing or a child-occupied facility built before 1978 is subject to the EPA Renovation, Repair and Painting rule, which requires a certified firm, a certified renovator on site, lead-safe work practices, and documented client notification.

Electrical Safety
OPTIONAL

Only qualified employees perform electrical work. The Company follows safe electrical work practices, guards live parts, uses ground-fault protection where required, and de-energizes circuits before work whenever feasible. Employees report damaged cords, outlets, and equipment.

Powered Industrial Trucks (Forklifts)
OPTIONAL

Only trained, evaluated, and authorized operators may operate forklifts and other powered industrial trucks. Operators perform pre-use inspections, follow safe operating rules, and observe pedestrian and load-handling precautions. Operator certification is renewed as required.

Aerial Lifts & Scissor Lifts
OPTIONAL

Only employees trained and authorized on the specific type of lift may operate one. Training covers the manufacturer's instructions, controls, load limits, hazards, and inspection, and is repeated after an accident, a near miss, a change of equipment, or observation of unsafe operation.

Before use. Complete a documented pre-use inspection of the controls, emergency lowering, guardrails, gates, tires, fluid levels, and warning devices, and a walkaround of the work area for holes, drop-offs, debris, slopes, overhead obstructions, and power lines. Defective lifts are tagged and removed from service.

Operation. In a boom-type aerial lift, employees wear a full body harness with a lanyard attached to the manufacturer's anchor point in the basket — never to an adjacent structure. In a scissor lift, the guardrail system is the fall protection; the gate or chain must be closed and employees must keep both feet on the platform floor. Never climb on or lean over the rails, never use a ladder or plank inside the platform to gain height, and never move an elevated lift unless the manufacturer permits it. Load and outreach limits are observed. Brakes are set and outriggers deployed where required.

Maintain minimum approach distance from energized lines; treat every line as energized unless the utility confirms otherwise.

First Aid & Medical Services
OPTIONAL

Where medical services are not in near proximity to the worksite, Sample 1 ensures that a person trained in first aid and CPR is available on each shift, and that adequate first aid supplies are readily accessible.

First aid kits are inspected before being sent to each job site and at least weekly on site, and are restocked immediately after use. Kit contents are appropriate to the hazards present. Where an employee may be exposed to injurious corrosive materials, an eyewash and quick-drench facility is provided within the work area for immediate emergency use.

Reporting. Every injury or illness, however minor, is reported to a supervisor before the end of the shift. Even minor cuts and strains are documented; a small injury reported late is the most common cause of a disputed claim. Employees are told where to obtain treatment and, where the state requires the employer to post or provide a designated provider list, that list is posted.

Emergency response. Each worksite has a posted emergency plan showing how to summon emergency services, the site address and nearest cross street, the location of the nearest emergency facility, and the assembly point. In a severe injury, call emergency services first, then notify a supervisor. Only trained responders provide care, using universal precautions and the personal protective equipment provided.

Workplace Violence Prevention
OPTIONAL

The Company maintains measures to prevent and respond to workplace violence, including reporting procedures, hazard assessment, and response planning. Some states (for example, California) require a written workplace violence prevention plan for many employers; where required, the Company maintains one.

Fleet & Driver Safety
OPTIONAL

Motor vehicle crashes are the leading cause of work-related death in the United States. Every employee who drives on Company business is expected to hold a valid license appropriate to the vehicle, maintain a satisfactory driving record, and follow this program.

Before driving. Complete the pre-trip inspection required for the vehicle: tires, lights, brakes, mirrors, fluids, wipers, horn, load securement, and required equipment. Report defects and do not operate a vehicle with a safety defect. Adjust seat and mirrors before moving.

While driving. Seat belts are worn by the driver and every occupant. Obey posted limits and adjust speed for weather, traffic, and load. No handheld phone use, texting, eating, or other distraction. No driving while impaired by alcohol, cannabis, illegal drugs, prescription medication that carries a warning, or fatigue. Maintain a following distance of at least four seconds, and more for heavy vehicles or poor conditions.

Loads and backing. Loads are secured and within the vehicle's rated capacity. Backing is avoided by parking to pull forward; where backing is necessary, walk the path first and use a spotter whenever one is available.

Incidents. Report every crash, no matter how minor, to a supervisor the same day. Stop, render aid, call law enforcement, photograph the scene, exchange information, and do not admit fault or discuss liability.
